newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares end a shade higher in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares end a shade higher in dull trade.

text.p: ** (1245) Shares across Indian bourses finish mixed in
lacklustre activity, poor market sentiment ** Market players stay away on absence of market moving news ** Benchmark Bombay bourse index ends 0.26 percent up as late
short-covering in pivotal stocks drives market upwards ** Madras index falls 0.69 percent, Madras index slids 0.69
percent, while Delhi index edges 1.03 points higher --
Shares across Indian bourses finished mixed on Thursday in dull trade as players stayed away from the market in absence of any market-moving news, traders said.
Brokers said short-covering and scattered buying by local funds helped select stocks end marginally higher.
"Short-covering by operators at close pushed up the market, but there was not much action in pivotals," said Dilip Joshi, a dealer at Bombay-based Prime Broking.
The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) Index was up 8.83 points at 3,391.54, or 0.26 percent after hitting a low of 3,348.75.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange Index falls 2.0 points, or 0.20 percent to 989.
The Calcutta index shed 0.23 points to 439.43 while the Delhi bourse index edged up 1.03 points at 757.41.
"Purchases by domestic and financial institutions reversed early trends and wiped out most of the losses," said Arun Aggarwal of Delhi-based brokers Jai Mata Securities.
Meanwhile, on Thursday the lower house of India's parliament approved the government's 1996/97 (April-March) Finance Bill by voice vote.

The finance bill included a controverial 12.9 percent minimum tax proposed by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram which aimed at targeting firms that paid no taxes by ploughing back profits into tax-spared dividends and diversifications.
Traders said sentiment had been affected as the market had expected the finance minister to provide some concessions in the minimum alternate tax to a few industries.

In pivotals, TISCO lost 0.25 rupees to 183.50, ACC 0.75 rupees to 2,024.25, and TELCO 5.50 to 459.75. Gainers included SBI up 4.25 rupees at 273, Gujarat Ambuja Cement 6.50 at 294, Hindustan Lever 2.25 at 824, Reliance 1.0 at 203.25 and MTNL 2.0 at 216.25. -- ANSHUMAN DAGA, Bombay newsroom +91-22 265 9000
